Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/rendering_pipeline_documentation.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/rendering_pipeline_documentation.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.

Retiam is built on a high-performance **WebGPU FrameGraph** rendering architecture. It supports 2D vector graphics (triangulated paths, SDFs, brushes) and full 3D PBR rasterization & cinematic raytracing in a single unified scene graph.

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
    A["Scene Composer (Scene Graph Traversal)"] --> B["Render Queue Packets (Entity + State + Geometry + Fragment)"]
    B --> C["Frustum Culling (Skip Off-Screen Entities)"]
    C --> D["Render Queue Depth Sort (Early-Z Front-to-Back)"]
    D --> E["RenderPass (Geometry & PBR Fragment Shading)"]
    E --> F["Shadow Pass (9-Tap PCF Depth24/32)"]
    E --> G["PPLL OIT / Standard Raster Compositor"]
    G --> H["Resolve / Super-Sampling (SSAA / MSAA)"]
    H --> I["Canvas Presentation"]

blocks.text: In traditional $[0 \rightarrow 1]$ depth buffers, half of the entire precision is wasted in the first 1% of the distance near the camera. In Reversed-Z, floating-point mantissa bits naturally match perspective division ($1/w$), providing **$100\times$ more depth precision** across massive draw distances and eliminating non-coplanar Z-fighting.
In WebGPU, `depthWriteEnabled` is an immutable, baked property of the pipeline state.

cells.text: Opaque models (Spheres, solid walls, boxes, pegs)

blocks.text: [`ModelFragment.prepare()`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/components/fragment/ModelFragment.ts#L15-L34) inspects the entity's material opacity and transmission:

items: **Result**: Transparent surfaces depth-test against solid walls, but **never write depth**, preventing objects behind them from being culled.

blocks.text: 3D models compute exact physical clip space positions directly from the 4x4 camera View-Projection matrix without 2D tree traversal depth biases:
Retiam features a zero-allocation, 6-plane frustum culling subsystem that eliminates off-screen draw calls and shading load.

blocks.code:
flowchart LR
    A["View-Projection Matrix"] --> B["Frustum.setFromMatrix()\n(Extracts 6 Planes: Left, Right, Top, Bottom, Near, Far)"]
    B --> C["RenderPass Packet Loop"]
    C --> D{"intersectsAABB(entityWorldBox)?"}
    D -- Yes --> E["Submit WebGPU Draw Call"]
    D -- No --> F["Instant Skip (0 GPU Cost)"]

items: **[`Frustum.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/math/Frustum.ts)**: Fast plane extraction from WebGPU $[0, 1]$ clip space and positive-vertex AABB intersection testing ($<5\text{ ns}$ per entity, 0 memory allocations).
**[`RenderView.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/camera/RenderView.ts#L65-L85)**: Maintains active `view.frustum` updated automatically with camera movement.
**[`RenderPass.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/passes/RenderPass.ts#L305-L318)**: Skips draw calls for culled objects.

blocks.text: To maximize frame rates across thousands of draw calls per frame:

children: Cached pipelines are looked up via `cyrb53` hash of the WGSL code + render state descriptor.
Tracks the active GPU pipeline, vertex buffers, and index buffers on the `GPURenderPassEncoder`.
Bypasses redundant driver calls if the same pipeline or buffer is already bound.

blocks.text: The 3D model fragment shader implements industry-standard Cook-Torrance microfacet specular and Lambertian diffuse shading:

items: **Fresnel**: Schlick's approximation with IOR / metallic blending.
**Shadows**: 9-tap Percentage-Closer Filtering (PCF) with normal-dependent adaptive bias.
**Tonemapping**: ACES Film Curve with $2.2$ gamma conversion.

cells.text: Super-Sampling Anti-Aliasing (renders at higher internal target resolution).
SSAA resolution scale multiplier ($2\times$ = 4× pixel area). Set to `1` for native resolution.
